answer.rationale: The strongest temporal signal is the release 2 hours ago followed by sustained write-path p99 degradation; inherited b1 says reverting a bad prior build cleared a customer-facing spike without impact, while b6 supports treating recent releases as prime suspects. Capacity, failover, circuit breakers, and read routing are less matched: peak load may contribute, but a release regression on the write path is more likely, and read replicas/failover do not directly protect heavy settlement writes. Rollback is disruptive during settlement peak and must avoid dropping in-flight writes, but it is the single intervention most likely to restore sustained availability if the new build is causative.
